title: PH hosts Melania Trump's global coalition for children's online safety, technology education
summary: First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos hosted on Monday the initiative for children's safety and empowerment, which was led by United States First Lady Melania Trump, on the sidelines of the 49th Association…

blocks.text: First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos hosted on Monday the initiative for children's safety and empowerment, which was led by United States First Lady Melanie Trump, on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

"Fostering the Future Together" is a global Coalition of First Spouses and equivalent leaders committed to helping children learn, grow, and thrive through safe and innovative use of advanced technology, including artificial intelligence.
During her speech in Pasay City, Araneta-Marcos said as technology opens opportunities, it also brings danger to children.
These dangers include cyberbullying, online exploitation, harmful content, and those taking advantage of children's innocence.

"We want our children to enjoy everything technology has to offer, but we also want them to be safe. And we certainly cannot expect them to navigate this complicated digital world all on their own," Araneta-Marcos said.
She added that the program has four pillars: artificial intelligence in education, education technology tools, online protection, and digital skills.

"The digital world, as you know, knows no borders, neither do the dangers that our children face. So I hope that today's conversation leads not only to the exchange of ideas, but to real partnerships and practical solutions that you can bring home to our respective communities and countries," Araneta-Marcos said.
In a video message, Melania Trump said the coalition aims to provide children tools to power the world's economy.

"Together, we can equip the next generation with the tools to power the world's economy (at scale) so that children in every corner of the planet can access and collaborate for prosperity, tolerance, and growth," Melanie Trump said.
"Let's leverage technology strategically so that every child's dream will be realized," she added.
Meanwhile, US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton said strong partnership is needed to ensure technologies are applied for the betterment of humanity, especially the children.
"This is an international cooperation for our kids, their educations, their safety, their future, and the kind of world we want to be leaving them," Lipton said in his speech.
Under the initiative, participating technology companies have committed to provide students all over the world with tools to adopt to emerging technologies.
As of 2026, the initiative has 57 participating countries, including France, Poland, UAE, Panama, Philippines, Israel, Morocco, and Turkiye. —KG, GMA News
